title: Meta’s Muse Tries (and Fails) to Disrupt Amazon
summary: Everyone loves a brawl between two big tech firms—even other tech CEOs. Amazon’s block on Meta Platforms’ new Muse personal agent accessing its shopping site, which came to light Sunday night, prompted Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora to post on X on Monday that the episode signals “a bigger battle than anyone anticipates.” He may be right: while Amazon has previously blocked Google and OpenAI shopping bots without drama, Amazon’s action against Meta is a bit more reminiscent of its blocking of Perplexity’s agent, which sparked a lawsuit that is still underway. And this is just the beginning. Arora, for instance, predicted that eventually everyone from Apple to Google and the AI firms will offer similar personal agents. title: World Models Need More Intelligence, Says Luma CEO Amit Jain
summary: The AI boom has been built largely on progress in language models, but a different approach has gained enormous attention in the industry this year: world models, which are designed to generate accurate predictions about the physical world, rather than words and numbers. I sat down with Amit Jain, co-founder and CEO of Luma AI, to discuss the promise of world models—and where current approaches to training them still fall short—on the latest episode of AI Deep Dive , The Information’s new show exploring the hard problems on tech’s frontier.
